questions.question: Explain why the Cost of Sales total from the CRJ is posted twice, and give both postings for Lindi's R3 000.
questions.expected_answer: Under the perpetual system every sale records the goods leaving at cost, so the monthly total must both record the expense and reduce the stock asset. Debit Cost of Sales R3 000 — the expense of the goods sold — and credit Trading Stock R3 000 — the shelf giving up those goods. The credit partners the Cost of Sales debit, never the Bank figure.

questions.question: Describe how to balance the Bank account for the month and interpret the result, using debits of R67 700 and credits of R25 300.
questions.expected_answer: Enter the difference of R42 400 on the smaller credit side as Balance c/d so both sides total R67 700, rule off, then bring the balance down on the debit side as Balance b/d R42 400. A debit balance on Bank means the business holds R42 400 in money.

questions.question: The trial balance does not balance. Describe the three diagnostic questions to ask before re-adding anything.
questions.expected_answer: Take the difference between the columns. If it equals one of your amounts, a posting was made once instead of twice. If it divides by two, an amount sits on the wrong side, since a side error doubles itself. If it divides by nine, digits were transposed — such as 4 200 captured as 2 400. Reading the gap first usually points straight at the error.
